newsitem.title: USA: SEC says three people settle "free-riding" charges.
newsitem.headline: SEC says three people settle "free-riding" charges.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission Wednesday said three individuals had settled the agency's charges against them for their alleged involvement in a free-riding scheme with more than 150 brokerage firms.

Without admitting or denying the allegations, Jury Matt Hansen and his wife, both of Bridgehampton, N.Y. and Fergus Sloan of New York City, agreed to be permanently barred from repeating the offenses and to turn over more than $11 million in alleged ill-gotten gains plus interest, the SEC said.
But all three were waived from making the payments based upon their financial condition, an SEC attorney handling the case said.
The practice of free-riding, when an individual buys then quickly sells stock without ever putting up any money, is a violation of federal law.
In its complaints dating back to 1989, the SEC alleged Hansen and Sloan opened more than 800 cash accounts at more than 150 brokerage firms using about 120 assumed names.
"Hansen and Sloan realized over $6 million in profits and caused hundreds of thousands of dollars in losses to the brokerage firms through which they traded," the SEC said.
Hansen had previously pleaded guilty to 10 counts of income tax fraud relating to an earlier free-riding scheme and been sentenced to one year in prison, the SEC attorney said.
Sloan pleaded guilty in 1975 to breaking securities laws and in 1992 he pleaded guilty to income tax fraud relating to the same free-riding case. He too was sentenced to prison.
